comments.body: Daemon half landed 2026-10-28 (83b17100..3f859db1): pane asking as daemon state (blocked/stuck, and a quiet helper whose maker cannot hear), presence from the app, Shown events, all on the internal protocol 1.9. Presence expiry settled: the app reports every 15 s, at once when Muster comes forward or goes behind and on use after 15 s unheard; each report lasts 45 s (daemon default 45 s, capped at 10 min) and ends when its connection closes. Reason: three heartbeats per report so one late report on a loaded machine never reads as the person gone; a hung app reads unknown within 45 s, a quit or crashed one at once. Written in docs/architecture.md. Known limit until stage 3: the daemon takes a maker on another machine as unable to hear, so a quiet helper of a devenv maker asks. The API attention topic is next.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

description:
MIP-10 stage 1, part 4 of 5: attention and presence. Read docs/mip/0010-api-for-other-tools.md sections 4 ("Attention") and 7.

What: what waits on the human, as state in the snapshot and as changes: each unread message that would ring the human (addressed to them, or rung by a group's policy) and each pane asking for them (blocked, stuck, or a quiet helper whose maker cannot hear it). Beside it, presence: the app reports to the daemon whether a window attends, whether Muster is in front, and when the person last used it, and the report expires after a set time so a crashed app reads as unknown. With the app quit there is no presence and attention still accumulates. When the app shows a banner or posts a notification it tells the daemon, which emits an informational event. Today those facts stay in the app (crates/muster-core/src/attention.rs, Sources/MusterMac/Notifications.swift) and the daemon knows only whether a window attends (crates/muster-daemon/src/session.rs). Touches the Swift shell and the core as well as the daemon. Settle the presence expiry (an open question in the MIP); record the answer on this card and in docs/architecture.md, since the accepted MIP is frozen.

Proves: with Muster quit, a post to @human appears as attention for a gate test client; a client restarting finds it still waiting; reading at the desk clears it; killing the app turns presence to unknown after the expiry.
title: MIP-10 stage 1d: attention and presence
